Newton's method as an abstract syntax tree

Source: R/codegen-algorithms.R
newtons_method.Rd

newtons_method(expr, wrt) builds the CodeBlock() of a Newton iteration solving expr == 0 for wrt, as SymPy's newtons_method(). newtons_method_function(expr, wrt) wraps it in a FunctionDefinition() returning the root.

Usage

newtons_method(
  expr,
  wrt,
  atol = 1e-12,
  delta = NULL,
  rtol = 4e-16,
  debug = FALSE,
  itermax = NULL,
  counter = NULL,
  delta_fn = function(e, x) -e/diff(e, x),
  cse = FALSE,
  handle_nan = NULL,
  bounds = NULL
)

newtons_method_function(
  expr,
  wrt,
  params = NULL,
  func_name = "newton",
  attrs = list(),
  delta = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

expr

The expression whose root is sought.

wrt

The symbol to solve for.

atol

The absolute tolerance.

delta

NULL (a Dummy() inside a Scope()), or the symbol of the step.

rtol

The relative tolerance.

debug

Whether to print the iterates.

itermax

NULL, or the largest number of iterations.

counter

NULL, or the symbol counting the iterations.

delta_fn

An R function of the expression and the variable giving the step; the default is the Newton step -e/diff(e, x).

cse

Whether to apply common subexpression elimination to the step.

handle_nan

NULL, or a node executed when the step is not a number.

bounds

NULL, or a list of the lower and upper bounds of wrt.

params

NULL (only wrt), or a list of the parameters (symbols, Variable() or Pointer() nodes).

func_name

The name of the function.

attrs

The attributes of the function.

...

Further arguments of newtons_method().

Value

A CodeBlock() (in a Scope() when delta is NULL), or for newtons_method_function() a FunctionDefinition().

Examples

x <- Symbol("x", real = TRUE)
algo <- newtons_method(cos(x) - x^3, x)
cat(ccode(newtons_method_function(cos(x) - x^3, x)), "\n")
#> double newton(double x){
#>    double d_x = INFINITY;
#>    while (fabs(d_x) > 3.9999999999999999e-16*fabs(x) + 9.9999999999999998e-13) {
#>       d_x = (pow(x, 3) - cos(x))/(-3*pow(x, 2) - sin(x));
#>       x += d_x;
#>    };
#>    return x;
#> }
